title: Protocol for targeting the magnocellular neuroendocrine cell ensemble via retrograde tracing from the posterior pituitary
protocol: Induce anesthesia in rats by intraperitoneal injection of an appropriate volume of anesthetics.
Wait 5-10 minutes and check responsiveness to nociceptive stimuli to ensure deep anesthesia.
Trim fur on the head with scissors.
Disinfect skin with three rounds of iodophor disinfectant followed by 75% ethanol.
Place the rat on the stereotaxic instruments.
Tuck ear bars into the ear canals loosely but stably.
Gently move the ear bars toward the center symmetrically.
Fit the up incisors into the tooth bar and slightly tighten the nose clamp.
Apply eye ointment to protect its eyes from strong illumination and prevent dryness.
Gently move the ear bars to avoid skull damage.
Ensure the rat head is horizontal to the base plate and vertical to the ear bars, allowing free up-down rotation only.
Cut the scalp from the middle of the eyes straight backwards to make a 10 mm incision.
Press the wound with wet cotton for 1-2 minutes if bleeding occurs to stop it.
Keep the skull moist with sterilized 0.9% saline throughout the surgery.
Clean the exposed skull with sterilized 0.9% saline-immersed cotton swabs followed by dry cotton swabs.
Display the Bregma and Lambda clearly on the cleaned skull.
Measure the AP, ML, and DV coordinates of the Bregma and Lambda with a dissecting microscope.
Adjust the tooth bar so that both the AP axis and ML axis of the skull are horizontal to the plate of stereotaxic instruments.
Set the coordinates of the Bregma as the origin (AP, 0 mm; ML, 0 mm; DV, 0 mm).
Mark the drilling point at (AP, -5.80 mm; ML, +0.05 mm) on the skull above the PPi.
Drill a bony hole in the SD rat skull using HM1 005 burs.
Rotate the AP and ML modulators to position the needle tip above the PPi.
Set the coordinates to (AP, −5.80 mm; ML, +0.05 mm).
Adjust the coordinates for rats weighing 220–300 g as needed.
Modify the ML coordinate to +0.05 – +0.10 mm to avoid sagittal suture damage.
Recommend the PPi coordinate (AP, −2.90 mm; ML, +0.05 mm; DV, −5.60 mm) for male mice aged 8 weeks and weighing 25 g.
Rotate the DV modulator to lower down the syringe until the tip touches the surface of the skull.
Mark the point with a thin marker pen under the dissecting microscope.
Uplift the DV modulator to leave space for drilling a bony hole.
Carefully drill through the skull bone at the marked point with a dental drill.
Drill until blood vessels beneath the skull are visible, but do not damage the brain parenchyma.
Do not apply downward pressure; rely on the self-gravity of the drill to thin the skull.
Drill slowly and suspend drilling periodically to clean bony powder with a rubber suction bulb.
Stop immediately upon feeling a hit pass as this indicates that the skull is drilled through.
Configure the microinjector to load 1200 nL AAVs at 1200 nL/min in withdraw mode.
Reload 20 nL air into the tip to avoid viral outflow.
Customize the syringe definition as 0.343 mm in diameter and 2.5 μL in volume if not preset.
Load an extra 200 nL AAVs to prevent paraffin liquid being infused into the PPi.
Wipe the residual paraffin on the outer wall of the needle before viral loading.
Reconfigure the withdraw mode to load an extra 20 nL air into the needle tip.
Clean the outer wall of the needle thoroughly with wet cotton swabs unidirectionally towards the needle tip to remove the residual virus.
Move the syringe back to the drilling point (AP, −5.80 mm; ML, +0.05 mm) so that the needle tip is close to the dura.
Penetrate the dura and slowly lower the syringe until the needle reaches the PPi (AP, −5.80 mm; ML, +0.05 mm; DV, −10.20 mm).
Infuse the virus at a low rate (70–100 nL/min, total 1020 nL including 20 nL air and 1000 nL AAVs) to the PPi.
Maintain the syringe at the position for another 10 min after infusion to allow viral diffusion and avoid viral backflow.
Uplift the syringe for 50 μm and maintain it for 3 min before full withdrawal.
Withdraw the syringe until the needle completely leaves the brain tissue.
Clean the needle tip immediately after withdrawal.
Wipe off any blood from the needle tip.
Apply drops of antibiotics to the craniotomy area.
Suture the craniotomy.
Disinfect the surgical area with 75% ethanol wipes.
Change the diaper for different rats during continuous operations of multiple rats.
Clean all surgical tools with three rounds application of iodophor disinfectant followed by 75% ethanol for every operation.
Monitor the rat in an isolated cage for 24 hours before sending it back to normal housing after surgery.
Perform post-operative monitoring of general conditions daily for 3–7 days, including physiological and behavioral states.
Ensure that rats eat, drink, and eliminate normally during recovery.
Measure and record post-operative body weight regularly.
Monitor the general appearance, grooming, posture, and locomotor activity of the rats.
Carefully scrutinize rats frequently curling up or exhibiting depressive behaviors.
Examine rats for signs of untreated pain or infection.
Check surgical sites for swelling and inflammation.
Look for signs of surgical complications such as pain, paralysis, and seizures.
Withdraw sutures 7 days after surgery from the wounds.
Allow the virus to express for 2–4 weeks.
